solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dishonest gent hiding right inside extremely full glider

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it tucked away within, so one piece goes inside another
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are wanted

parts.note: the two end letters of 'full'
a lying person is dishonest

indicators.note: whatever is inside a frame sits between its walls, so a run of letters goes within an outer pair

parts.note: a squire is a country gentleman
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A crooked gentleman stows away inside a fully loaded glider aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glider' suggests an aircraft, but it is an animal. 'Extremely full' keeps only the two ends of that word, which then wrap around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: This small rodent spreads skin flaps between its limbs and glides from tree to tree, so naturalists class it as a glider.

clue.text: Eagerly left Swedish giant's house ahead of time

indicators.note: being ahead of something means coming before it, so these parts are placed in sequence

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
IKEA is the giant Swedish furniture retailer; the possessive adds S
HO is the abbreviation for house
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly abandoned the Swedish furniture giant's showroom before closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of IKEA'S is kept as a letter, giving L + IKEA + S + HO + T.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something like a shot is an idiom for doing it at once and with enthusiasm, without hesitation.

clue.text: Runner not out with regulars from northbound squad

indicators.note: with simply attaches one part to the next in sequence

parts.note: a batsman who is not out is still in

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
regular letters are those taken at even intervals, here every other one starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of 'squad'

explanation.surface: A cricket runner who survived, alongside the usual members of a team heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' and 'not out' both suggest cricket, but a runner is a river in crosswords. In cricket a batsman who is not out is still 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers run, so crossword setters often call one a runner; this great river flows through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Leave sizeable article on the German duck

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the parts follow each other in order

parts.note: to go is to leave
OS stands for outsize, a label for big clothing
an is the indefinite article
der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave a big item placed on top of a German's duck.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is the clothing-size label for large garments; DER is the German masculine 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: This large sawbill with a narrow serrated beak is a species of diving waterfowl, a kind of merganser.

clue.text: Odd bringing in note for Republican man on board

indicators.note: bringing in one thing for another means swapping a newcomer into the place of an existing letter

parts.note: queer in its old sense means odd or strange
N is the abbreviation for note
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A strange business: a note arriving in place of a Republican crew member on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of QUEER is swapped for N. 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; chess pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are traditionally called men, and this most powerful piece is one of them on the chessboard.

clue.text: Gut section 9 spanning river after 13.00

indicators.note: coming after means following in sequence, so this part is placed second

parts.note: 13.00 on the 24-hour clock is one o'clock, and one is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: to span something is to stretch right across it, so one piece reaches around another

parts.note: the number written out as a word
the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

explanation.surface: A stretch of gut, like a section of a bridge numbered nine crossing a river after lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9-down, but here it is just the number, spelt out. 'Section' belongs with 'Gut' in the definition, and the Test is an English chalk-stream river.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowel is the part of the alimentary canal below the stomach, one section of the whole digestive tract or gut.

clue.text: Scope operated on middle of ridgeway

indicators.note: in a down clue, one part on another sits above it, so they follow in order

parts.note: to run a machine is to operate it

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of 'ridgeway'

explanation.surface: A telescope or rifle sight in use along a long hilltop path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope' and 'operated' suggest a device being used; 'Scope' is the definition and 'operated' only gives RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the extent or breadth something covers, as in the range or scope of an inquiry.

clue.text: Altered angle as Mamma's serving?

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mamma has changed her approach to serving, or is that her dish?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mamma' with two Ms is the Italian spelling, pointing to Italian home cooking; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: This layered pasta bake is a classic Italian dish, just what an Italian mother might put on the table.

clue.text: Fresh green American incense

indicators.note: a fresh version is a new one, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A new type of green-scented American joss stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the noun for fragrant sticks, but it is the verb meaning to anger, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious, which is exactly what this verb means: to fill with fury.

clue.text: Uncovered wound on doffing of cap

indicators.note: doffing a cap removes what sits on top, so the first letter comes off

parts.note: a road that wound has snaked along

explanation.surface: A head left bare and an injury exposed when a hat is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, as a path winds or snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left bare with no clothing or covering is described as both naked and uncovered.

clue.text: 50pc of binary code preceded by clear hints

indicators.note: being preceded by something means coming after it, so the parts are placed in sequence

parts.note: something overt is plain and clear
binary code is made of ones and zeros, so half of it is the ones

explanation.surface: Half a stream of computer code follows some obvious clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Binary uses only two digits, 0 and 1, so '50pc' of it is one of those two kinds of digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle suggestions or implications beneath what is said, which makes them hints.

clue.text: Lake region a lass on vacation visits

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: an area is a region
taken as written

indicators.note: vacating a place empties it, so the inner letters go and only the outer ones stay

parts.note: 'lass' with its middle letters removed

explanation.surface: A young woman on holiday tours the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake region' suggests England's Lake District, but 'Lake' alone is the definition; despite its name, this sea is a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite its name this body of water in Central Asia is a landlocked saline lake, now greatly shrunk by irrigation.

clue.text: Reserve twisting leg gets enough nurses

indicators.note: twisting turns something round, so these letters are read backwards
to nurse is to hold closely, so the words cradle the letters within them

parts.note: the letters running across the end of 'leg', all of 'gets' and the start of 'enough'

explanation.surface: A sprained leg gets plenty of care from the nurses on the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is read backwards from 'enough' through 'gets' into 'leg'. 'Nurses' looks like the hospital staff, but it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Savings kept aside for the future are a nest egg, money held back as a reserve for later.

clue.text: Drunk European recalled drinking hard spirit

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters go back the way they came
drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
E is the abbreviation for European
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A drunken European, remembered for drinking hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is the noun, a drunkard, not the adjective; 'hard spirit' suggests strong liquor, but 'spirit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ethos of a group is its characteristic character, values and outlook, which is its spirit.

clue.text: Picture kit to make booze at front of magazine

indicators.note: being at the front means coming first, so the parts are placed in order

parts.note: a still is apparatus for distilling spirits
Life was a famous American photo magazine

explanation.surface: A photo of home-brewing equipment on a magazine's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' looks like it belongs with the magazine image, but it is the definition, standing for a type of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting or picture of inanimate objects such as fruit, flowers or vessels arranged on a table.

clue.text: Scatter last of chilli on slate with foie gras for one

indicators.note: in an across clue, one part on another follows it, so they are placed in sequence

parts.note: to diss is to criticise harshly, as to slate does

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of 'chilli'
foie gras is one example of pâté

explanation.surface: A chef sprinkles the end of some chilli onto a slate platter with foie gras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' looks like the serving board, but it is the verb meaning criticise. 'For one' marks foie gras as an example of the pâté category.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissipate is to disperse or cause to vanish in many directions, which is to scatter.

clue.text: Pencils in school Leeds university fabricated

indicators.note: something fabricated is made up or constructed, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Pencils at a Leeds school and university turn out to be fakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pencils' looks like a plural noun, but 'Pencils in' is a verb phrase. Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To pencil something in is to book it provisionally on a calendar, which is a way of planning or timetabling it.

clue.text: Small soldier breaking silver coating of useless spears?

indicators.note: something breaking into another bursts inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
S is the abbreviation for small
a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: a coating covers only the outside, so just the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of 'useless'

explanation.surface: A little soldier smashes through the silver plating on some useless spears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spears' suggests weapons, but the question mark signals the vegetable's shoots. Ag, from Latin argentum, is the chemical symbol for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible young shoots of this vegetable are sold and cooked as spears, so the plural word stands for the plant.

clue.text: She has power test curtailed amid protest?

indicators.note: being amid something means in the middle of it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: curtailing cuts short, literally docking the tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A woman in authority is cut short in a trial during a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing a person rather than a single word, and 'test' is the piece being docked.
explanation.definitionFit: The female head of a family or community holds authority over it, so she is a woman with power.

clue.text: Little Asian leader oddly chummy

parts.note: Narendra Modi is the prime minister of India

indicators.note: oddly means at the odd positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are taken

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of 'chummy'

explanation.surface: A short Asian head of state who is strangely friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' looks like an adjective describing the leader, but it is the definition, used as a noun meaning a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small quantity of something, as in 'a little sense', so the noun matches 'a little'.

clue.text: Retired half of chapel drive out

parts.note: an ex-player is a former, retired one

indicators.note: half of a word is one of its two equal parts, here the second, so only those letters stay

parts.note: the second half of 'chapel'

explanation.surface: A retired churchgoer takes half the congregation for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: EX means former, as in ex-wife, which is how 'retired' gets there.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to force someone or something to leave, such as a pupil from school, which is driving them away.

clue.text: Delivered instruction for shrink

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a lesson is a piece of instruction

explanation.surface: Directions given out to a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like slang for a psychiatrist, but it is the verb meaning reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to make or become smaller, so it is a verb meaning reduce in size or amount.

clue.text: Did tinker fish with line in river channel?

indicators.note: with simply joins one part onto the next in sequence

parts.note: a dab is a flatfish

indicators.note: being in something means going within it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a riverbed is the channel a river runs in
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A tinker went fishing with a line in a river's channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like a noun for a travelling mender, but 'Did tinker' is a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dabble is to take part in something casually or superficially, much as tinkering means fiddling with it.

clue.text: Not a single taxi around enclosed bit of Sandwich?

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the letters are read back to front

parts.note: no as in 'no taxi', not a single one
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Not one taxi to be found anywhere near the enclosed part of Sandwich, a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent, but the capital letter is a disguise for the food; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers of this cured pork are a classic filling placed between slices of bread in a sandwich.

clue.text: Charlie in LA cut plant inhabiting centre of sandbank

indicators.note: inhabiting a place is living inside it, so one piece goes within another
the centre of a word is its middle letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of 'sandbank'

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a weed is a plant

explanation.surface: A man in Los Angeles cuts a plant growing in the middle of a sandbank.
explanation.walkthrough: A Charlie is British slang for a fool; 'in LA' asks for the American equivalent rather than a person living in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a dweeb is a boring, socially awkward person, the US counterpart of a British Charlie or twit.

clue.text: Splits roles after editor retreated

indicators.note: coming after means following in sequence, so this part is placed second
retreating means going backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
actors' roles are parts

explanation.surface: Responsibilities are divided up once the newspaper editor has backed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splits' looks like it divides the roles, but it is slang for leaves, as in 'I'm splitting'.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is informal slang for leaving a place, and someone who leaves departs.

clue.text: Pervert turned up with new cocktail ingredient

indicators.note: with simply joins one part onto the next in sequence
in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to warp is to pervert or distort
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A deviant showed up with a novel addition to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail' suggests a drink, but the prawn cocktail is a classic British starter of shellfish in a pink sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish is the main component of a prawn cocktail, a retro seafood starter served in a glass.

clue.text: Dye calico when tipsy without wife

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters are thrown into disorder
without means lacking something, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife, the letter taken away

explanation.surface: Someone dyes calico cloth while drunk, without his wife around.
explanation.walkthrough: W is the standard abbreviation for wife; calico is a plain cotton fabric, fitting the dyeing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This crimson colouring made from crushed scale insects is a natural dye, used in food and fabrics.

clue.text: Fever overwhelming king in dispute

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf completely, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An illness strikes down a monarch during a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: AGUE is a crossword staple for fever, and R comes from Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute a point is to contest it with reasons and counter-claims, which is to argue it.

clue.text: Mischief working main vehicle among pits with son

indicators.note: with simply joins one part onto the next in sequence
being among things means sitting in their midst, so one run goes inside another

parts.note: pits are mines
a machine that is on is working
the main point is the key point
a bus is a vehicle
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Trouble at the colliery: a main transport vehicle running among the pits, with a boy aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like a noun for a pipe or the sea, but it is the adjective meaning chief, as in the key issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for playful or dishonest behaviour, the sort of trickery that counts as mischief.
